items.rationale: A new session starts with an empty window and the model keeps nothing from earlier calls; only saved notes could bring Monday back. Options b and c show the belief that the model or window remembers across sessions.

Call 1 sends 1,050; call 2 sends 1,050 + 500 = 1,550; call 3 sends 1,550 + 100 = 1,650. Total 1,050 + 1,550 + 1,650 = 4,250. An answer of 1,650 counts only the longest call (the peak), not the sum; 1,650 shows the cost is misread as the peak.

Retrieval brings only the relevant pages into the window, so you pay for about two pages and the answer comes from your manuals. Option a and d pay for 200 pages on every call and invite context rot; option c answers from training, not your manuals.

items.answer: It goes stale: availability changes, so a saved copy would be wrong later; the calendar should be asked each time.
accepted: it will be out of date
the calendar is the source of truth

items.rationale: Notes are for lasting facts. Availability changes, and a stale note could cause a double booking.

items.answer: Compact: summarize the conversation and restart with the summary, or clear old tool results.
accepted: summarise the conversation and continue with the summary
items.rationale: Either compaction (summary replaces history) or clearing old tool results frees the window. A bigger window alone, or doing nothing, is not an answer.
